title: Why hot air rises
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How does a hot air balloon fly?

explain.say: Hot air rises because it is lighter than the same amount of cooler air around it. A bubble of warm air is pushed up, just like a cork in water.
When air is heated, its particles move faster and spread further apart. The same air now takes up more room, so it is less dense.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Warming air makes it less dense

explain.say: The surrounding cooler air pushes up on the warm bubble with a force called upthrust. Because the warm air weighs less than the cool air it pushes aside, upthrust beats its weight and it rises.
As the warm air rises it spreads and cools, until its weight matches the upthrust and it stops. A hot air balloon uses this: its burner keeps the air inside hot, so it floats up.

faq.q: Why is hot air lighter than cold air?
faq.a: Heating makes air particles move faster and spread out, so a litre of hot air holds fewer particles and weighs less than a litre of cold air.
Upthrust is the upward push a liquid or gas gives anything sitting in it. It equals the weight of the fluid pushed aside, so things lighter than that weight float up.

faq.q: How does a hot air balloon fly?
faq.a: A burner heats the air inside the balloon, often to around 100 degrees Celsius. That hot air is so much lighter than the cool air outside that the upthrust lifts the balloon, basket and passengers.
asks: Why do hot air balloons float?

faq.a: Warm air from heaters and people rises and collects near ceilings and upper floors, while cooler, denser air sinks to the ground floor.
Not exactly. Heat spreads in every direction. What rises is warm air or water, because it is less dense than the cooler fluid around it.
asks: Is it true that heat rises?

facts: Warming air by about 30 degrees Celsius makes it roughly 10 percent less dense.
The first crewed hot air balloon flight, in a Montgolfier balloon, took place over Paris in 1783.

options.show: It is less dense, so upthrust beats its weight
options.say: It is less dense, so upthrust beats its weight

quiz.why: Warm air weighs less than the cool air it pushes aside, so the upthrust on it is bigger than its weight.

wrong.0: Warm air does have weight, just less than the same volume of cool air.
wrong.2: There are no separate heat particles; it is the warm air itself that rises.
